title: R' Chutzpit, the Public Interpreter (Meturgeman)
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He was the public interpreter (meturgeman) in the Sanhedrin of Yavneh under the patriarchate of Rabban Gamliel, as related in Bekhorot 36a in the incident of R' Tzadok, when all the people murmured and they said to him, “Stop.” Likewise in Berakhot 27b, when they removed Rabban Gamliel from his patriarchate, they said to him, “Stop.”
In the Jerusalem Talmud there, chapter 4, end of halakhah 1, the wording is that they said to him, “Dismiss the people.”

He is mentioned in Mishnah Sheviit 10:6 as R' Chutzpit without further designation: he says, “One writes [a prozbul] for a person on his wife’s property,” etc. Tosefta Kelim, Bava Batra 2:1, relates that Rabbi Chutzpit, R' Yeshevav, Rabbi Chalafta and Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri sat [in secret] in Tzippori with Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah.

Hyman reports that he was one of those executed by the government, as stated explicitly in Eichah Rabbati, chapter 2, on “He swallowed,” and Midrash Tehillim 9:13. He was then a hundred and thirty years old, as cited in the Midrash Eleh Ezkerah printed in Beit HaMidrash, part 2. He was not given burial, as stated explicitly in Kiddushin 39a and the end of Chullin: Elisha, Acher, saw the tongue of Chutzpit the meturgeman being dragged by a “davar acher” [a pig]; he said, “Shall the mouth that brought forth pearls lick the dust?” So too it is cited in Tosafot on Bekhorot 36a that he was one of those executed by the government.
In the Or Zarua, Hilkhot Bekhorot, he wrote that he was equal to Yonatan ben Uzziel.

Tosefta Kelim Batra 2:1 places the four elders with Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah in Tzippori. The Sefaria Community Translation takes חרש to mean “in secret.” The brackets mark that interpretation. The artisans appear later in a separate case on the Temple Mount. Rash MiShantz on Kelim 22:9 quotes a version that places the meeting in Rabbi Elazar’s shop, prints חרש in parentheses, and calls Chutzpit “the interpreter.” The earlier note records the source question before this reassessment.
